axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.assessment: Final covers U1–U6 as a standalone proposal: separate identities and content-backed local journal; recovery from process/network/source changes; two mechanisms; three integrity levels; accountable cleanup/retry owners; versioned history and exact compatibility tuple; facts/design/unknowns and proposed/executed separation. Existing UI and identity stay outside implementation scope. Conditional gateway journaling respects the preference to avoid a second durable server, while retaining tus. No real upload or throughput result is asserted. The original brief's phase/reveal constraints are assessed separately as protocol evidence.

axis_coverage.name: Consequential source claims and exact applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: Primary checking confirms bounded tus offsets/extensions, AWS part/response/cleanup rules and sizing, checksum algorithm/type distinctions, and specific MinIO/Go history. Final distinguishes PutObject reproduction from Rust UploadPart and part body from encoded frames. Policies and provider enablement remain conditional. No remaining material factual error or unsupported consequential selection was found. Minor source-map errors label a proposal commit as the PR head and locate a PR relationship under the issue's Development panel; both are independently resolved in reviewer evidence without changing original files.

axis_coverage.name: Useful discovery, alternatives, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axis_coverage.assessment: Discovery adds useful mechanisms beyond the initial user draft: tus HEAD/PATCH reconciliation with conditional extensions; numbered MPU retry/reconciliation; non-MD5 ETags/composite checksums; embedded completion errors; configured lifecycle versus application deadline; versioned wire-encoding incompatibility. Two required transports are compared by storage/state/bandwidth burden. Meaningful related options include direct versus gateway-proxied parts, full-checksum versus readback, and snapshot/locking as explicitly undecided local-identity options. The MinIO issue, unmerged proposal and pinned Go default change provide relevant history. Breadth is adequate for one bounded transfer; no extra protocol/product survey is invented as an obligation.

axis_coverage.name: Wrong criticisms/corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axis_coverage.assessment: All criticism IDs C1/C2/E1 have explicit final dispositions. C2 identifies a genuine draft cleanup-procedure gap across expiry/orphans and is resolved in final. C1's mechanism distinction is correct; its material severity is stronger than the draft supports, because the draft already denies a demonstrated 16 MiB workaround and gates wire encoding. Treat it as clarified ambiguity rather than a proven material false recommendation. Final's acceptance causes no unsupported repair. E1 retains honest external uncertainty. Largest-part-only resume, ETag-as-file-proof, and completion-call-only done are appropriately corrected. Every exact released-plan paragraph and its constituent clauses is assessed below.

axis_coverage.name: Supported meaning preserved through discovery/draft/critique/final
axis_coverage.assessment: The final preserves the transfer-only boundary, both transports, conditional gateway/direct path, content manifest/spooled exact bytes, whole-file recheck, identity binding, noncontiguous recovery, completion/integrity levels, cancel winner semantics, expiry/orphan owners, lifecycle uncertainty, history limits and unrun validation status. Preliminary 64 MiB discovery arithmetic is explicitly superseded by the released 16 MiB preference, with both arithmetic bases retained. Serial start changes a nonbinding concurrency preference while preserving the ceiling of three. The final adds encryption profiling and unified cleanup without treating a proposed deployment as existent. C2's original lineage gap remains documented rather than erased.

axis_coverage.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: Six final matrix rows have observable invariants and integration limits: lost/noncontiguous part outcomes; changed-source and spool races; delayed/error completion; cancel/expiry/orphan/live-grant races; principal/grant expiry; exact profile sizes/wire/checksum behavior. Fake tests can inspect state/journal/fencing decisions but cannot prove a real provider's durability, parser, checksum or grant-drain behavior. The final explicitly leaves those for exact-endpoint integration. FULL_OBJECT comparison is conditional on matching algorithm/type; AWS multipart SHA-256 does not satisfy that route, so readback or accurately unverified status is needed. No model, fake transport, upload, readback or throughput test is asserted as executed. Source/reveal review is not empirical transfer validation.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: I lean toward letting the desktop client send multipart pieces directly, with the existing gateway granting permission. A service implementing a resumable HTTP protocol is the alternative. I would like to avoid introducing a second durable server if the storage API is sufficient, but I have not established that it is.
constituent_clause_dispositions: Direct client parts with existing gateway permission: retained conditionally; grant drain must be qualified, otherwise proxy/defer.
Resumable HTTP service alternative: tus retained with offset/persistence/storage tradeoff.
Avoid second durable server if storage API sufficient; sufficiency unknown: native-first candidate and explicit gateway capability question, no assertion existing gateway already supports it.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: Draft sequence: ask the gateway for a transfer identity; split the file into 16 MiB pieces; save a local JSON record with the remote identity, filename, file size, modification time, and piece numbers. Upload pieces with at most three concurrent requests. After restart, continue from the largest saved piece number; I have not addressed noncontiguous successful pieces. Call the completion operation and mark the job done. These sizes and concurrency limits are preferences, not measured optima.
constituent_clause_dispositions: Ask gateway for transfer identity: client idempotency ID, gateway session, unique key/provider ID are distinct.
16 MiB pieces: retained as application candidate; not a wire frame limit or tested workaround.

Local JSON with remote identity, filename/size/mtime/piece numbers: opaque session, source path/length/fast metadata, part set, hashes/ranges and profile/state; raw store ID retained at gateway. Filename is metadata, not overwrite key.
At most three concurrent requests: retained ceiling; serial start is a declared original choice.
Resume largest saved piece; noncontiguous gap: rejected as insufficient, entire qualified remote set reconciled.
Call completion and mark done: refined to parsed/reconciled completed object plus integrity state, not mere request/HTTP success.
Sizes/concurrency preferences, not measured optima: explicitly preserved.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: I was assuming an ETag could serve as the file's integrity check. I do not know how that assumption changes for multipart uploads, encryption, or a compatible vendor. The plan also does not yet say how a lost response is distinguished from a failed operation. Please resolve those issues without silently choosing weaker integrity guarantees.
constituent_clause_dispositions: ETag file-integrity assumption: corrected; opaque ETag is not whole-file SHA-256 proof.
Multipart/encryption/vendor applicability unknown: composite/full distinction, encryption mode profile and vendor gate; no generic S3-compatible assertion.
Lost reply versus failed operation: RECONCILING, same identity/key/part and source bytes, parsed completion/status.
No silent weaker guarantee: independent byte-match, transfer-checks-only and unverified are distinguished; no checksum-disabling workaround is chosen.

exact_plan_dispositions.exact_text: Keep the UI to progress, retry, and cancel. On cancellation I want remote temporary data removed, but the cleanup actor and retry behavior are undecided. Gateway token expiry during an upload is also undecided. A stale recovery file must never cause bytes from a changed source file to be accepted as the original upload. Do not store credentials in that recovery file.
constituent_clause_dispositions: Progress/retry/cancel UI only: existing UI implementation remains outside scope; transfer states are inputs to it.
Remote temporary removal on cancel; actor/retry undecided: gateway fenced/drained/re-abort/list procedure, durable unresolved outcome, completed-object winner separate.
Gateway token expiry undecided: existing host reauthentication and same-principal renewal; grant versus session expiry separate.
Stale recovery must not accept changed bytes as original: whole-file digest on resume/finalization plus each spooled range; mismatch blocks old-session completion and requires explicit new intent.
No credentials in record: retained and strengthened to no tokens/signed URLs; recovery is not authorization.

Preserve the option of a protocol service if research supports it; the initial preference is not a command to reject it. The final plan needs a minimal state sketch, one owner for each recovery/cleanup action, and an explicit compatibility boundary. It does not need executable product code.
constituent_clause_dispositions: U1–U6/negative constraints binding: all six separately inspected; negative constraints separately listed.
Protocol service remains possible; preference does not reject it: retained tus conditional alternative.
Minimal state sketch: PREPARED/INITIATING/UPLOADING/FINALIZING/COMPLETED, reconciliation and distinct stop causes.
One owner each action: client local data/body retries; gateway session/reconciliation/cleanup; store API execution; host existing credentials; operator lifecycle configuration.
Explicit compatibility boundary: vendor/build/bucket/endpoint/SDK/wire/checksum/cleanup tuple; disabled until tested.
No executable product code required: proposal only, no nonexistent implementation demanded.
